title: Relative approximation of a formal isomorphism with a varying base map
statement: Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $S$ and $T$ are of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Let $x\in X$, $s\in S$, $y\in Y$, and $t\in T$ satisfy $x\mapsto s$ and $y\mapsto t$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and let $\sigma:\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\widehat A$ be a local ring homomorphism (it sends the maximal ideal into that of $\widehat A$). Completions here and below are maximal-ideal-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Form $Y_\sigma=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ [def-pc-fibre-product], using $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}\to T$. Suppose $y_\sigma\in Y_\sigma$ maps to $y$ and to the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, and an isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y_\sigma,y_\sigma}$ of $\widehat A$-algebras is given. Then there exist a pointed étale morphism $(V,v)\to(S,s)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a morphism $\tau:V\to T$ with $\tau(v)=t$, and a scheme $U$ with point $u$, equipped with an étale morphism $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ and an étale $V$-morphism $U\to Y\times_{T,\tau}V$. The maps commute over $S$ and $V$, and $u\mapsto v$. The induced maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(v)$ and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$ [def-weil-residue-field] are isomorphisms. No equality of the resulting formal map with the original formal isomorphism is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, specialized to a base S of finite type over the integers (whose local rings are G-rings).

proof.text: Restrict $S,T$ to affine neighbourhoods of $s,t$, and $X,Y$ to affine neighbourhoods of $x,y$ mapping into them. This is the affine-local form of the finite type hypotheses. A diagram for these restrictions gives one for the originals: open immersions and composites of étale maps are étale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Stalks and their scalar maps at the marked points are unchanged.

Apply [lem-trf-completed-base-affine-etale-span] to the given scalar-compatible formal isomorphism. With $B=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, this gives $x_B$, an affine finitely presented $H/B$, and a pointed étale span $X_B\leftarrow H\to Y_\sigma$ with both residue maps isomorphisms. The canonical maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(b)$ and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x_B)$ are isomorphisms. Use the map $\lambda:B\to T$ induced by $\sigma$.

Apply [lem-trf-varying-base-smooth-span-model] to this span and $\lambda$. Obtain a smooth $S'\to S$, $r:B\to S'$, and $\lambda':S'\to T$ factoring $\lambda$, together with the pointed span $X'=X\times_SS'\leftarrow H'\to Y'=Y\times_TS'$. At $s'=r(b)$, $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')$ is an isomorphism; the lemma also gives residue isomorphisms for both stage arrows and $\kappa(x')\to\kappa(x_B)$. Since $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x')\to\kappa(x_B)$ is the canonical map from step 2, $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x')$ is an isomorphism. Moreover $\lambda'(s')=t$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-span-etale-slice] to these two stage arrows at $h'$. All its residue hypotheses were verified in step 3. It supplies $V\to S$, $\tau=\lambda'|_V$, and $W=H'\times_{S'}V$ with marked points $v,w$. Its canonical arrows $W\to X$ and $W\to Y\times_{T,\tau}V$ are étale and commute over the required bases; $w\mapsto x,v$, $\tau(v)=t$, and the induced maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(v)$ and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(w)$ are isomorphisms. Taking $(U,u)=(W,w)$ proves the assertion.
